newsitem.title: DENMARK: OSCE sets September 13-14 for Bosnia local election.
newsitem.headline: OSCE sets September 13-14 for Bosnia local election.

text.p: The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) confirmed on Thursday that Bosnia's local elections, originally planned for mid-July, would be postponed by two months.

"I as Chairman-in-Office of the OSCE have decided that the municipal elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina should take place on September 13 and 14," a statement from Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen said.
Petersen said that he had made his decision on the recommendations of the OSCE mission to Bosnia and with the agreement of EU and NATO colleagues.
He said the success of the polls depended largely on the behaviour of local political groups.

"In this context the Chairman-in-Office urges the local parties to ensure, in particular, freedom of movement, equal access to free media and prompt installation of democratically elected officials," the statement said.

The local polls were originally to be held in September 1996, along with general elections, but were postponed because of widespread election fraud over refugee registration to November 1996 and then to July this year.
Western countries funding the election had been pushing for a further postponement of the vote to allow more time to organise refugee registration and international monitoring.
The 54-member OSCE, Europe's top security body, is in charge of organising the elections, viewed as Bosnia's last chance for reunification after a devastating 43-month war.
Officials say the OSCE needs up to $55 million to organise the vote. The next round of nationwide elections are set for 1998, one year after the municipal vote in September.
